raw.title: v0.3.0
raw.body:
## Feature Release — `arazzo test`, sourceDescriptions auto-load, explicit transport trust

The three headline changes: a CI-native `test` command, `operationId` resolution straight from your spec's `sourceDescriptions` (no `--openapi` flag), and transport behavior that is now chosen rather than inherited — scoped TLS exceptions, an explicit redirect policy, and a transport warnings model.

### ⚠️ Behavior change
- **https→http downgrade redirects are now refused by default.** Previous releases silently followed them (an inherited HTTP-client default). A refused downgrade fails the step with `RUNTIME_REDIRECT_DOWNGRADE_REFUSED`, naming both URLs; pass `--allow-downgrade-redirects` to restore the old behavior. Same-scheme redirects behave exactly as before (pinned by characterization tests), and the hop limit is unchanged at 10 (`--max-redirects` to adjust).

### `arazzo test` — CI-native contract testing
- **Recursively discovers** `.arazzo.yaml`/`.arazzo.yml` specs and executes every workflow
- **TAP output by default**, JUnit XML via `--format junit`, structured JSON via `--json`
- **Full flag parity with `run`**, plus `--fail-fast` and `--filter <regex>`; exits non-zero on any failure

### sourceDescriptions auto-load (#3)
- **Relative `type: openapi` sourceDescriptions are loaded at engine build**: `operationId` steps resolve and the request base derives from the document's `servers[0].url` — `run`, `test`, the MCP server, and the debugger all pick this up with no `--openapi` flag
- **Failures are loud and named** (source + resolved path), never a silent fallback; explicit `--openapi` specs still win duplicate operationIds with a warning

### Transport trust
- **`--insecure-host <host[:port]>`** (repeatable, on `run` and `test`): accept an untrusted certificate for exactly that host — every other host in the run keeps full verification. Blanket `--insecure` exists for curl `-k` parity, but the scoped form is the point: one workflow run touches many hosts, and a self-signed localhost cert shouldn't weaken your production calls. Certificate failures now name the host and this exact remedy.
- **Transport warnings, stderr only**: a startup notice listing active insecure exceptions, a once-per-host warning when `Authorization`/`Cookie` headers travel over non-loopback cleartext `http://`, and an end-of-run note naming exceptions no request used (stale-flag detection for Makefiles/CI). `--no-transport-warnings` / `ARAZZO_NO_TRANSPORT_WARNINGS=1` silence the text — structured `transportWarnings` entries persist in `--json` envelopes and traces, because degraded-trust facts are audit data.
- **Redirect chains are visible**: followed hops are recorded in trace output (`request.redirects`) and survive into trace files and replay.

### Arazzo 1.1 groundwork
- **Typed 1.1 model**: AsyncAPI source descriptions, selector objects, async step metadata, and `$message.*` expressions parse, validate, and round-trip
- **Async execution fails closed** with `RUNTIME_UNSUPPORTED_ASYNCAPI_TRANSPORT` before any HTTP request — metadata is preserved, transport execution is future work

### Agent ergonomics
- **"For agents" help sections** on root and subcommands; `schema <command>` output contracts; `warnings` array in `run --json`
- **`--version` flag** (finally — thanks @erwinkramer)

### Generator
- **OpenAPI 3.1/3.2 input is detected** and reported with an actionable message instead of a cryptic deserialization error; full 3.1/3.2 ingestion is tracked in #3

### Fixes & security
- JSONPath: unsupported constructs surface diagnostics instead of silently evaluating false; count-predicate tokenization fixed
- Engine: filtered `--step` goto semantics, action `type` override preservation, generator `$ref` cycle guards
- Dependency advisories cleared, including `rustls-webpki` (RUSTSEC-2026-0104/-0098/-0099) in the shipped binary; `cargo audit` is clean

Full details in the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/strefethen/arazzo-cli/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
